Reversing 1200 gives 0021, and numbers have no leading zeros, so it is 21. Trailing zeros vanish when reversed.

questions.q: Counting digits with while (n > 0): what goes wrong for n = 0?
questions.e: The loop never runs for 0, so the count stays 0. Handle 0 separately, or use a do-while loop.
In C++, % takes the sign of the left number, so the last digit of a negative number comes out negative. Take abs() first.

questions.q: The product of the digits should start at:
questions.e: Starting at 0 would make every product 0. 1 is the “nothing yet” value for multiplication.

questions.q: What is the digital root of 38 (add the digits until one digit is left)?
Why save a copy of n before the digit loop?
questions.e: n / 10 runs until n is 0, so the original value is gone. Palindrome and Armstrong checks need it after the loop.

questions.q: Which is an Armstrong number (each digit raised to the number of digits, added up, gives the number)?
questions.e: 1³ + 5³ + 3³ = 1 + 125 + 27 = 153. 145 is a Strong number (1! + 4! + 5!), not an Armstrong number.
